items.title: 68145_Jimmie Rowles oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Jimmie Rowles) narrates Art Tatum's relationship with Slam Stewart ('Slam Stewart was the first bass player he had ever played that could talk with him... I'm going to form a trio now.') but does not describe a direct personal or professional relationship between himself and Slam St

ctx.x: We worked in a place called the Capri. And we had Big Joe Turner singin' the Blues, and Ray Bryant was dancing, and we traded off sets, you know, with Lee and Lester Young and Slim and Sam's band, alternating with Spirits of Rhythm with Teddy Bunn and Leo Watson, and Big Joe Turner was singing with them... I got to know an awful lot of people. Ben Webster used to come in. I had met Ben previously in Seattle, and we became very close, and he used to come out there all the time and play with us. And he kept telling…

We switched clubs, and moved down to Fairfax and Beverly into a place called the Trouville, and they changed everything all around. It became Lee and Lester Young's band without Slim and Sam. That's where I met Red Callender and Louis Gonzales, a guitar player, and a trumpet player from St. Louis who used to be with Basie, Paul Campbell, and Lester and Bumps, Lee, and me -- we were the band. Slim and Slam played alone, and the Spirits of Rhythm played alone,
